statement: Let S be the byte string obtained by concatenating source[0], a newline byte, source[1], a newline byte, ..., a newline byte, source[len(source)-1]. Scan S from left to right starting in state NORMAL and building a byte string C initially empty. In NORMAL: if the next two bytes are '/' '/' then consume them and switch to LINE; otherwise if the next two bytes are '/' '*' then consume them and switch to BLOCK; otherwise append the next byte to C and advance one byte. In LINE: if the next byte is a newline then append it to C, advance, and switch to NORMAL; otherwise consume the next byte without appending. In BLOCK: if the next two bytes are '*' '/' then consume them and switch to NORMAL; otherwise consume the next byte without appending (including a newline byte). A two-byte test fails if fewer than two bytes remain. The scan stops when all of S is consumed (it never stops in BLOCK by the precondition). Let r be the list of byte strings obtained by splitting C at every newline byte and then deleting all empty byte strings, preserving order. The function returns r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(source) <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < len(source), len(source[i]) <= 80; every block comment opened during the scan of source is eventually closed (equivalently, the scan never ends in the block-comment state).
